clinician.final_diagnosis: acute PK secondary to an acute spontaneous idiopathic left renal subcapsular hematoma that became infected
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old female with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus presented with urinary symptoms, left flank pain, fever, and hyperglycemia. Initial renal ultrasound was normal. Abdominal CT without contrast during hospitalization revealed a left renal subcapsular hematoma (3.8 x 5.4 x 8.3 cm). Urine culture grew Candida glabrata confirming urinary tract infection. Symptoms improved during hospitalization. Outpatient CT showed interval growth of the subcapsular hematoma with gas foci indicating infection. She was treated empirically with piperacillin/tazobactam, narrowed to ceftriaxone after Klebsiella pneumoniae was cultured. Percutaneous drainage of the left renal abscess yielded 500 mL of pus, with near-complete abscess resolution on post-procedure imaging. Persistent flank pain and hypertension were documented at follow-up. The constellation of imaging, microbiological cultures, intervention, and clinical course supports acute pyelonephritis secondary to infection of an idiopathic left renal subcapsular hematoma.
